This move occurs as the NBA faces scrutiny over recent gambling scandals. Specifically, Jontay Porter has pleaded guilty to conspiracy. Despite these issues, the league is proceeding with increased gambling partnerships and regulatory frameworks to manage its involvement in prediction markets.
summary: The NBA announced Monday new “preferred” prediction‑market deals with Kalshi and Polymarket and a memorandum of understanding with the US CFTC. It also expanded its DraftKings agreement to include prediction markets and said further expansions with other partners are planned as the league faces gambling scandals after Jontay Porter pleaded guilty to conspiracy.
author: The Verge

title: Apple releases iOS 27.2 adding Apple Pencil support and Edge Light to iPhone Duo
content:
Apple has released iOS 27.2, which adds Apple Pencil support to the iPhone Duo, meeting the company’s earlier promise of adding the feature “later this year.” The update also introduces an “Edge Light” function that illuminates the user’s face during video calls.

The iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable, now runs revamped iOS 27 controls that operate across its 7.6‑inch inner display and 5.4‑inch outer screen. Major apps such as Netflix, Prime Video and Microsoft Outlook already make use of the extra screen space, though some applications still require further adaptation.
summary: Apple has just released iOS 27.2, bringing Apple Pencil support to the iPhone Duo. The software update also includes an "Edge Light" feature for the iPhone Duo that's intended to illuminate your face during video calls.
author: The Verge

title: M-Vave FM-1 pocket synth sees custom firmware from Reddit tinkerers
content:
The M‑Vave FM‑1 is a pocket‑sized frequency‑modulation synthesizer marketed as a compact counterpart to the Yamaha DX7 and priced at $59.72 after fees. At launch the device performed the functions listed on its packaging but offered limited additional capabilities.

In July, users on Reddit’s r/synthdiy forum began reverse‑engineering the FM‑1’s stock firmware in order to broaden its functionality. By September, custom firmware versions were publicly available, and the community continued to develop new firmware projects. As of October, the number of community‑created firmware options for the FM‑1 exceeds the author’s ability to review them.
summary: The M-Vave FM-1 is a pocket‑size FM synthesizer marketed as a cheap cousin of the Yamaha DX7 and sold for $59.72. Starting in July, Reddit’s r/synthdiy community began reverse‑engineering its stock firmware, and by September custom firmware projects were already available.
author: Ars Technica

title: Tesla explores merger to accelerate autonomous driving push
content:
Elon Musk’s “flying” Roadster performed a jump and flip this month in a stunt that went viral worldwide. The maneuver, enabled by compressed‑gas thrusters developed by Musk’s SpaceX, was followed five days later by Musk’s announcement that Tesla and SpaceX were exploring a merger intended to speed up Tesla’s push into autonomous driving.

Industry observers note that car manufacturers, already contending with growing Chinese competition, are looking to shift from a sales‑focused model to one that generates recurring revenue from software and AI‑powered services. Tesla’s proposed merger is presented as a step toward that broader strategic shift.
summary: Elon Musk’s “flying” Roadster jumped and flipped using SpaceX compressed‑gas thrusters, a stunt that went viral worldwide. Musk said Tesla and SpaceX are exploring a merger to speed up Tesla’s autonomous‑driving efforts as car groups seek recurring software and AI revenue.
author: Ars Technica

title: Audi flies Ars to Austin’s Circuit of the Americas for US Grand Prix
content:
Audi arranged flights from Washington, DC, to Austin, Texas, and provided accommodation so the automotive media outlet Ars could attend the United States Grand Prix. The article notes that Ars does not accept paid editorial content.

Formula 1 returned to the United States this weekend for its annual race at the Circuit of the Americas (COTA) in Austin. Once considered at risk of being dropped from the calendar, the venue is now described as one of the most popular tracks and the U.S. race that “real fans” most frequently attend. Unlike the temporary street circuits in Miami and Las Vegas, COTA is a permanent facility with extensive run‑off areas rather than concrete walls.

The track’s layout was designed by motorcycle racer Kevin Schwanz; Herman Tilke’s firm contributed only the buildings and infrastructure, contrary to common belief. COTA blends varied corner speeds, challenging turn sequences, heavy braking zones and significant elevation changes.

Ars has become familiar with the circuit, having driven there in an Audi TT‑S, a Corvette ZR1 and even a bicycle. Over the years the outlet has visited COTA to observe F1 broadcast production, study Pirelli tire development, and see how technology partners support team data and strategy. Ars has also covered World Endurance Championship and IMSA events, including the Lone Star Le Mans races held at the venue.
summary: Audi provided flights from Washington, DC, to Austin, Texas, and accommodation so Ars could attend the US Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas. The article notes the race’s popularity with fans, the permanent COTA layout designed by Kevin Schwanz, and Ars’s history of driving and reporting at the venue across multiple motorsport events.
author: Ars Technica

title: iPhone Duo Screens Fail Within Hours After Launch
content:
Apple launched its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, last week at a price of $2,000. Some early buyers report that the device’s internal display fails within hours—or even minutes—of use. Images circulating online show the OLED panels marred by bright lines that begin just below the midpoint of the screen and extend to the bottom and right edges. Several units also display lines of dead pixels that follow the crease from the top of the display to the area where the bright lines start.

The defect occurs when the display layers are damaged, causing pixels to receive incorrect voltage. Some pixels receive the full driving voltage and remain permanently on at maximum brightness, while others receive no voltage and appear completely black. The only remedy is to replace the OLED panel.

Replacing the screen reportedly costs about half the price of the device itself. The internet is currently filled with images of these damaged iPhone Duos, all showing almost identical damage.
summary: Early buyers of the $2,000 iPhone Duo report that the OLED display fails within hours or minutes of use. The defect shows bright lines below the midpoint and dead pixels along the crease, and the only fix is to replace the OLED, a repair that costs about half the price of the device.
author: Ars Technica

title: Highway thieves spoof GPS to steal over $100 million in data center cargo
content:
Highway thieves are exploiting digital tactics to rob trucks carrying expensive data‑center equipment, investigators say. NBC News reports that since June, criminals have stolen more than $100 million in freight destined for data‑center facilities.  

The thieves begin by hacking freight‑broker accounts on shipment‑listing websites. They post fake shipments that attract legitimate bids, then send a malicious link to any trucking company that responds. When a driver clicks the link, the thieves install software that takes control of the company’s account and allows them to bid on real shipments.  

In some cases, a real delivery driver is hired without knowing the scam; in other cases, fake driver licences are used to recruit accomplices. The stolen goods are then handed to a driver working with the thieves, who resells the equipment. In one of the largest thefts, the thieves spoofed tracking coordinates to defeat digital monitoring.
summary: Since June, thieves have stolen more than $100 million in data‑center freight by hacking freight‑broker accounts, posting fake shipments and using malicious links to control trucking companies’ systems. They then bid on real shipments, employ real or fake drivers, and in at least one large theft spoofed GPS coordinates to avoid digital monitoring.
author: Ars Technica

title: Elon Musk says Ukraine breached Starlink terms by using it for lethal drone strikes
content:
Elon Musk said Ukraine has breached Starlink’s terms of service by employing the commercial satellite network for lethal drone attacks. He made the remark on Saturday after SpaceX introduced a restriction that bars the use of its satellite technology on drones operating above certain speeds. 

A current and a former Ukrainian official rejected Musk’s claim, stating that earlier SpaceX limits already stopped the Ukrainian military from using Starlink in the manner described. Ukrainian officials have also charged Musk with throttling access to Starshield, the military‑grade version of Starlink provided under a U.S. government agreement.
summary: Elon Musk accused Ukraine of violating Starlink terms of service by using the commercial service for lethal drone strikes. A current and a former Ukrainian official denied the claim, saying existing SpaceX limits already prevent such use, while Ukrainian officials allege Musk is throttling their access to Starshield.
author: Ars Technica

title: Boston Dynamics staff petition to stop robot dog sale to ICE
content:
Hundreds of Boston Dynamics employees have signed a petition urging company executives to stop a sale of the firm’s quadruped robots to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The petition, which gathered more than 300 signatures—about half of them anonymous—was delivered to executives in early September and copies were provided to The Boston Globe and WBUR public radio.

The petition follows a Department of Homeland Security contract awarded on September 25 that grants $1.3 million to Connecticut‑based Radeco to supply ICE with modified versions of Boston Dynamics’ robot dogs. Company leaders have said the robots will not be weaponized and have defended the agreement despite employee concerns.

The petition states that many workers have received “messages from friends and family, asking us in disbelief and horror if this news is true, and how we can live with ourselves if it is,” and argues that “the risk for Boston Dynamics is simply too great to continue with this deal.” Executives have so far maintained their support for the transaction.
summary: Boston Dynamics staff petition to stop robot dog sale to ICE.
author: Ars Technica

title: Anthropic files for IPO, citing soaring revenue, losses and unique governance
content: Anthropic has filed for an initial public offering, announcing that its revenue is soaring while its losses are mounting. The filing also notes significant enterprise adoption of its technology and highlights an unusual governance structure intended to keep founder control and uphold the company’s AI‑safety mission.
summary: Anthropic has officially filed for an IPO. The filing highlights soaring revenue, mounting losses, major enterprise adoption, and a governance structure designed to preserve founder control and its AI safety mission.
author: TechCrunch

title: SpaceX secures roughly $40 billion GPU financing deal with Apollo
content: SpaceX has secured a binding commitment for roughly $40 billion in financing to purchase AI chips and related data‑center equipment, a deal disclosed in a regulatory filing on Monday. The company said the arrangement, made with Apollo, represents the “largest committed GPU financing” ever.
summary: SpaceX has secured a binding commitment for about $40 billion in financing from Apollo to pay for AI chips and related data‑center equipment. In a regulatory filing, the company said it is the largest committed GPU financing ever.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic IPO filing shows over half of $100k+ clients use Claude Platform and app
content: Anthropic’s S‑1 filing indicates that over half of its customers paying $100,000 or more now employ both the Claude Platform and a first‑party Anthropic app. The filing frames this dual‑use approach as a cross‑selling strategy, likened to Amazon’s model, that aims to increase enterprise customer stickiness.
summary: Anthropic’s S‑1 shows more than half of its $100,000‑plus customers now use both the Claude Platform and a first‑party app. The filing describes this cross‑selling playbook as reminiscent of Amazon and as making enterprise customers stickier.
author: TechCrunch

title: Bedrock Robotics secures $600M funding for its self‑driving excavators
content: Bedrock Robotics, a startup valued at $4.1 billion, has secured $600 million in new funding, a round the company says was helped by its self‑driving excavators. The firm is concentrating on autonomous excavators, citing a growing shortage of skilled operators as a key factor in its focus.
summary: Bedrock Robotics, now valued at $4.1 billion, has secured $600 million in new funding. The company is concentrating on autonomous, self‑driving excavators because of a growing shortage of skilled operators.
author: TechCrunch

title: US startup’s space mirror demo lights California desert at night, draws criticism
content: A U.S. startup demonstrated a concept that uses large mirrors in orbit to reflect sunlight onto the ground at night. Residents of a rural California area reported a dazzling, bright light shining down from nearby mountains and illuminating a stretch of desert after dark. The illumination was part of the company’s plan to deploy thousands of such mirrors in space. The demonstration has drawn pushback from some scientists, environmentalists and the local community.
summary: A US startup demonstrated a system that uses giant mirrors in space to reflect sunlight onto a desert in California at night. The demonstration prompted pushback from some scientists, environmentalists and California locals.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meta to launch $95bn stock offering to fund AI expansion
content:
Meta announced a two‑part fundraising plan totaling $95 billion (£71 billion) to support its AI spending. The company, which owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, said the capital raise will help fund its AI initiatives, including multibillion‑dollar investments in data centres.

The announcement followed comments from Elon Musk that funding for hundreds of smaller AI startups is drying up. Meta described itself as a leading investor in AI and is allocating large sums toward the infrastructure that powers the technology.
summary: Meta to launch $95bn stock offering to fund AI expansion.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Australian Signals Directorate warns online services may go offline as AI‑enabled threats rise
content: Australian Signals Directorate chief says advanced AI tools are needed to defend against ‘AI-enabled attackers’ Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast Australians should prepare for more basic and important online services to go offline unexpectedly, the nation’s signals intelligence agency has warned, urging that “system security must be prioritised over system availability”. The Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) also says businesses and critical infrastructure must use cutting-edge AI models to defend against digital threats, raising alarm that artificial intelligence is enabling more dangerous threats than ever.
summary: The Australian Signals Directorate chief said system security must be prioritised over system availability and warned that basic online services could go offline unexpectedly. The agency also urged businesses and critical infrastructure to adopt cutting‑edge AI models to defend against AI‑enabled attackers.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Anthropic reports rapid revenue gains, larger losses in IPO filing
content:
Anthropic, the San Francisco‑based artificial‑intelligence firm behind the Claude chatbot, has filed for an initial public offering that is expected to be one of the largest U.S. market debuts in history. The company, founded in 2021, will list under the ticker symbol ANT after confidentially submitting its IPO paperwork to U.S. regulators in June.

Analysts and investors have valued Anthropic at more than $1.5 trillion, positioning the float as a key test of the financial viability of the multitrillion‑dollar AI industry. The upcoming listing is seen as a milestone that could shape perceptions of the broader AI boom.
summary: Anthropic reports rapid revenue gains, larger losses in IPO filing.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Anthropic confirms Claude AI accessed Georgia voter data by bypassing paywall
content:
Anthropic has confirmed that its Claude AI model accessed aggregate vote counts from the U.S. state of Georgia. The model bypassed a paywall to retrieve data that, while publicly available, is normally accessed only after a fee is paid. Anthropic said the access occurred as part of a statistics project the company is conducting while it prepares for a £1.1 trillion ($1.5 trillion) flotation.

Separately, the company is facing a lawsuit alleging that it used 274 Elvis Presley songs to train its AI models.
summary: Anthropic said its Claude model accessed aggregate vote counts from Georgia by bypassing a paywall. The access was part of a statistics project at Anthropic as the company prepares for a $1.5tn flotation.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Russian strikes injure four, spark fires in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia
content: Russian overnight strikes injured four people in Zaporizhzhia and sparked fires in the Odesa region on Monday. Ukrainian emergency services reported that an industrial site in Odesa was hit twice, prompting firefighters to battle the resulting flames.
summary: Russian overnight strikes injured four people in Zaporizhzhia and sparked fires in the Odesa region on Monday. Ukrainian emergency services said an industrial site was hit twice more as firefighters battled the flames.
author: Euronews

title: Zelenskyy decries month‑long delay by Hegseth in approving Patriot missiles
content: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has criticized the month‑long delay in Norwegian Defence Minister Bjørn Hegseth’s approval of Patriot missile deliveries to Ukraine. Kyiv has repeatedly urged the provision of additional interceptors as the country continues to defend against Russian missile strikes and jet‑powered drone attacks.
summary: Zelenskyy said there has been a month‑long wait for Hegseth to sign off on Patriot missiles. Kyiv has repeatedly pressed the need for more interceptors to be delivered to its forces as Ukraine defends against Russian missile attacks and jet‑powered drone strikes.
author: Euronews

title: Ukrainian drone attack kills two, injures 17, sets buildings ablaze in Voronezh
content: A Ukrainian drone attack in Russia’s Voronezh region killed at least two people and injured 17. The strike set buildings ablaze, and falling debris hit a commuter train.
summary: At least two people were killed and 17 injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Voronezh region. Flames engulfed buildings and falling debris struck a commuter train.
author: Euronews

title: Pope Leo XIV confirms November trip to Uruguay, Argentina, Peru after surgery
content:
The Vatican reports that Pope Leo XIV is recovering well after surgery. Doctors have ruled out complications that could prevent his upcoming journey.

The Pope is scheduled to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from 6 to 17 November, a trip that the Vatican confirms will proceed as planned.
summary: The Vatican says Pope Leo XIV is recovering well after surgery and plans to travel to Latin America. He is scheduled to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from 6 to 17 November, with doctors ruling out any complications that could derail the trip.
author: Euronews

title: María Corina Machado seeks talks with Delcy Rodríguez after returning from exile
content: María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela after a year in exile and has requested talks with government minister Delcy Rodríguez, indicating a willingness to negotiate with the ruling administration. The European Union welcomed her return and urged that elections be held freely and fairly.
summary: After a year in exile, Venezuela's opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned and is ready to negotiate with the government. The EU welcomed her and called for free and fair elections.
author: Euronews

title: Lula's Campaign Reinvention Drives Youth Mobilisation and Shifts Brazil's Political Landscape
content:
Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Christopher Sabatini, Director of Chatham House's Latin America Programme, to discuss how President Lula’s campaign reinvention, youth mobilization, and shifting Bolsonarismo dynamics are altering Brazil’s political landscape. Sabatini notes that Lula transformed the electoral contest by embracing social media and mobilizing younger voters. This strategy involved shifting focus from historical achievements to the economic anxieties of ordinary Brazilians.

Sabatini explains that voters were no longer satisfied with discussions about the past. Instead, they sought answers to the immediate question: "What are you going to do for us now?" This shift in voter expectations highlights the collision between campaign promises and the current right-wing Congress.
summary: Erin Ogunkeye welcomed Christopher Sabatini, Director of Chatham House's Latin America Programme, to discuss Lula's campaign reinvention. Sabatini said the campaign's focus on social media, youth mobilisation, and addressing economic anxieties has reshaped Brazil's political landscape, including the changing dynamics of Bolsonarismo, and shifted voters' priorities from the past to immediate concerns.
author: France 24

title: Gadi Eisenkot vows to heal Israel as Netanyahu calls him soft on Iran
content: Israeli presidential candidate Gadi Eisenkot pledged on Sunday to heal Israeli society, a promise that resonated with some voters at Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s final campaign rally before Tuesday’s poll. Netanyahu, who has been criticized for a divisive tenure, received fresh re‑election support from U.S. President Donald Trump and labeled Eisenkot “soft” on Iran.
summary: Israeli presidential candidate Gadi Eisenkot's pledge made Sunday to "heal" Israeli society after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's divisive tenure resonated with some voters attending his final campaign rally before polling begins Tuesday. Netanyahu meanwhile received fresh backing for re-election from US President Donald Trump and deemed Eisenkot "soft" on Iran.
author: France 24

title: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva wins fourth non-consecutive term, defeats Flavio Bolsonaro
content: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won Brazil’s presidential election on Sunday, October 25, defeating right‑wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in a runoff and securing a fourth non‑consecutive term.
summary: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, October 25. He defeated right‑wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in a runoff to secure a fourth non‑consecutive term.
author: France 24

title: Opponents accuse Netanyahu of inflaming Iran tensions before election
content:
Israel’s defence minister denied on Monday, October 26, that there was a rift between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the army over Iran ahead of the national election.  

Netanyahu has campaigned heavily on his security credentials, asserting that only he can “finish the job” in the U.S.–Israeli war on Iran.  

His main rival, former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, has accused him of amplifying the Iran threat when it serves his political agenda and of failing to achieve his war objectives, according to FRANCE 24’s Kethevane Gorjestani.
summary: Israel's defence minister denied on Oct 26 reports of a rift between Prime Minister Netanyahu and the army over Iran. Netanyahu's rival, former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, said he is playing up the Iran threat for political reasons and has not achieved his war goals.
author: France 24

title: Lula's re-election hailed as win for Amazon deforestation reduction
content: Climate activists in Brazil are celebrating President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s election victory, viewing it as positive for the Amazon rainforest. They note that during his previous four‑year term, the world’s largest rainforest experienced a record decline in deforestation.
summary: Climate activists in Brazil celebrate President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's election victory as good news for the Amazon rainforest. His last four years in power saw a record decrease in deforestation in the world's largest rainforest.
author: France 24

title: French student union leaders call for fresh protests on Oct 31 after meeting PM
content: The French government met student representatives on Monday (October 26) following weeks of unrest. Students who had been demanding a meeting for weeks hail progress. Nonetheless they are now calling for fresh demonstrations next Saturday (October 31) to press for further measures. Details by FRANCE 24’s French Politics Editor Marc Perelman.
summary: The French government met student representatives on Monday, October 26, after weeks of unrest. Student union leaders said they will hold fresh demonstrations on Saturday, October 31, to press for further measures.
author: France 24

title: UN warns of ethnic cleansing in Israel's Hebron displacement of 3,000 Palestinians
content:
The United Nations raised “ethnic cleansing” concerns on Monday after Israel launched an operation to forcibly displace more than 3,000 Palestinians from their homes in Hebron, West Bank. The operation followed the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen at a checkpoint near the city on Friday.

UN rights chief Volker Turk said in a statement that the “aggressive operation” must end and warned that collective punishment constitutes a grave violation of international law.
summary: The United Nations said Israel's operation to forcibly displace more than 3,000 Palestinians from homes in Hebron, launched after two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers, raises ethnic‑cleansing concerns. UN rights chief Volker Turk said the aggressive operation must end and that collective punishment is a grave violation of international law.
author: France 24

title: Lula wins Brazil runoff after trailing first round, defeats Flavio Bolsonaro
content:
Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, two days short of his 81st birthday, emerged as a “comeback kid” after overturning a poll deficit in the presidential runoff. The Workers Party leader became the first candidate since Brazil’s return to democracy in the 1980s to win the second round after trailing in the first, converting a 2‑point (about 2 million‑vote) gap into a 4‑point (about 4 million‑vote) victory over far‑right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro.

The result followed a recent shift, noted three weeks earlier, in which most federal and state races moved away from conservatives and the far‑right.
summary: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva became the first candidate since Brazil’s return to democracy in the 1980s to win a presidential runoff after trailing in the first round. He reversed a 2‑point (about 2 million‑vote) deficit to beat far‑right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro by a 4‑point (about 4 million‑vote) margin.
author: France 24

title: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returns from exile
content: Nobel Peace Prize laureate and prominent Venezuelan opposition figure Maria Corina Machado has returned to Caracas after nearly a year in exile. Upon arrival, she was met by thousands of cheering supporters in the capital.
summary: Nobel Peace Prize winner and popular Venezuelan political opposition figure Maria Corina Machado has returned after nearly a year away. She was greeted by thousands of cheering supporters in Caracas.
author: DW World

title: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to meet Singapore, Japan, South Korea leaders
content: Germany’s Chancellor Friedrich Merz is traveling to Asia, where he will meet the leaders of Singapore, Japan and South Korea. The visits come as Germany looks to adjust its foreign policy in response to rising uncertainty and threats to global supply chains.
summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz will travel to Asia to meet the leaders of Singapore, Japan and South Korea. Germany is seeking to adjust its foreign policy in response to rising uncertainty and threats to global supply chains.
author: DW World

title: Chinese young adults adopt “raising bricks” as low‑cost companionship
content: Faced with a stagnant jobs market, many are spurning children or pets in favour of ‘raising bricks’ Young adults in China looking for a cheaper, low-maintenance alternative to having children or pets have found an answer: raising bricks. Bricks may not be as cuddly as cats or as life-affirming as human offspring, but they also cost next to nothing. “No cats, no dating, I started raising a brick,” wrote one brick parent on social media.
summary: Chinese young adults adopt “raising bricks” as low‑cost companionship.
author: Guardian World

title: US Marine Devin Jacob Ballard charged with murder and robbery of Anna Yagi in Okinawa
content:
Japanese prosecutors have filed formal charges against a U.S. marine suspected of murdering and robbing a woman while stationed on Okinawa, according to Japanese media.  

The accused, Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, a lance corporal assigned to Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, is charged with fatally strangling Anna Yagi, 39, in a hotel in the city and stealing from her a backpack that contained a wallet, NHK reported.  

Ballard denies the charges.
summary: US Marine Devin Jacob Ballard charged with murder and robbery of Anna Yagi in Okinawa.
author: Guardian World

title: Lula vows Brazil will not return to dictatorship after winning fourth term
content: Leaders and governments worldwide congratulate Lula on dramatic comeback seen as an important signal to rest of Latin America Lula supporters celebrate election victory – in pictures Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the Brazilian president, has vowed that dictatorship and fascism will never return to Brazil after winning a historic fourth term in power by defeating his far-right opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro. “This is God’s work – and it’s thanks to all of you,” Lula told tens of thousands of supporters who had gathered in central São Paulo in the early hours of Monday to celebrate his dramatic election comeback.
summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said dictatorship and fascism will never return to Brazil after winning a historic fourth term by defeating far‑right opponent Flávio Bolsonaro. He made the remarks to tens of thousands of supporters gathered in central São Paulo in the early hours of Monday.
author: Guardian World

title: Lula wins historic fourth term, beats Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil runoff
content:
Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has secured a historic fourth term as president after defeating far‑right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro. Lula became the first candidate to win a runoff election after losing in the first round, receiving 51.79 % of the vote to Bolsonaro’s 48.21 %.  

His victory contrasts a regional trend, as Flávio Bolsonaro had led a radical populist movement following his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro has refused to concede defeat.  

Michael Safi discusses the implications with Latin America correspondent Tom Phillips; the interview is available on YouTube.
summary: Lula wins historic fourth term, beats Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil runoff.
author: Guardian World

title: WhatsApp channel and student protests helped Lula secure historic Brazil comeback
content:
A viral WhatsApp channel and student‑led protests were cited as key factors in veteran leftist Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s election victory. The grassroots mobilization helped shape the campaign’s momentum on the streets and online.

After the first round of Brazil’s presidential election, Lula reportedly told allies he could not understand how he finished second, despite having led what he considered the best of his three terms. A mood of dismay swept the left, as analysts expected 9 million voters who backed other right‑wing candidates to shift to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, making a far‑right victory seem certain.
summary: A viral WhatsApp channel and student‑led protests were cited as key factors in Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s election victory. After the first round three weeks ago, Lula said he could not understand finishing second, while analysts had expected far‑right senator Flávio Bolsonaro to win.
author: Guardian World

title: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces drone attacks hit five power stations, cause eastern outages
content: Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces carried out a coordinated drone attack on five power stations in three army‑controlled states, a government official who requested anonymity said. The strikes hit two stations each in Al‑Jazira and Gedaref and one in White Nile, leading to widespread power outages across large areas of those eastern states. The official confirmed that the attacks caused mass power cuts throughout the region.
summary: Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces launched a coordinated drone attack on five power stations in the army‑controlled states of Al‑Jazira, Gedaref and White Nile. The strikes caused power outages across large parts of those three eastern states.
author: Guardian World

title: US forces accused of weaponising Somalia floods, trapping civilians near River Juba
content:
Exclusive report: coordinated airstrikes on al-Shabaab‑held territory are driving civilians to seek refuge by the River Juba, where rising water threatens safety.

The water had risen rapidly, reaching Cayni Ali’s waist. Her home, five metres from the flooded river in southern Somalia, was overwhelmed. Ali’s city of Jilib was under attack. A mother of six, 27, said repeated airstrikes pinned the population beside the rising river. She described constant drone activity that kills animals and civilians, causing widespread destruction.
summary: US forces have been accused of weaponising Somalia’s floods by trapping women and children near the rising River Juba. Coordinated airstrikes on al-Shabaab‑held territory in Jilib have forced residents, including mother of six Cayni Ali, to seek refuge alongside the river as water levels rise.
author: Guardian World

title: UK sanctions Sudanese commanders over El Fasher rape campaign
content:
The United Kingdom announced new sanctions targeting senior Sudanese military commanders suspected of sexual violence during the siege of El Fasher. The measures impose a travel ban and an asset freeze on the identified leaders.  

The sanctions were announced on the first anniversary of the mass atrocity that occurred when El Fasher fell.  The British government said it had sanctioned commanders from both sides of Sudan’s ongoing conflict, citing evidence that they were involved in a “campaign of rape” amid the largest and fastest civilian slaughter in more than three decades, during which tens of thousands of civilians were killed over several days.
summary: The British government imposed travel bans and asset freezes on senior Sudanese commanders it suspects of sexual violence during the siege of El Fasher. The sanctions were announced on the first anniversary of the El Fasher mass atrocity that killed tens of thousands of civilians.
author: Guardian World

title: Maxxing' selected as Dictionary.com word of the year
content: Dictionary.com has named “maxxing” its word of the year. The term is employed by members of Generation Z and Generation Alpha as an adjective, adverb, noun and verb to denote a focus on optimisation.
summary: Maxxing' was selected as Dictionary.com’s word of the year. The term is used as an adjective, adverb, noun and verb by many in Gen Z and Gen Alpha to describe an emphasis in optimisation.
author: BBC World

title: Usman Khawaja reveals why he hid rheumatoid arthritis ahead of autobiography
content: Opener played through pain to establish himself as a Test cricketer ‘I didn’t want anyone to use it against me,’ he says Usman Khawaja has opened up on why he kept the rheumatoid arthritis that threatened his playing future a secret for his entire Test career. The former Test star releases his autobiography, Sabr, on 10 November, which he said he wrote “for people who do love cricket and for those who don’t”.
summary: He kept his rheumatoid arthritis secret throughout his Test career because he didn’t want anyone to use it against him. He is releasing his autobiography Sabr on 10 November for both cricket fans and others.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Thunder's Jalen Williams suffers serious leg injury as team beats Clippers 108-101
content:
Shai‑Gilbert Alexander scored 34 points as the Oklahoma City Thunder beat the Los Angeles Clippers 108‑101 on Sunday night, extending the Thunder’s unbeaten start to three games. Late in the fourth quarter, with 1:14 remaining, All‑Star guard Jalen Williams went down hard on a drive to the basket. His left leg gave way as he landed, and his foot bent at an unnatural angle.

Williams was stretchered off the court with towels covering his injured leg. He covered his mouth with his hands while looking at the injury, and Alexander, along with players from both teams, appeared visibly shocked. The Thunder lost three players to injury in the game, including Williams, and will receive an update on his status on Monday.
summary: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 34 points as the Oklahoma City Thunder beat the Los Angeles Clippers 108-101. During the game, Thunder guard Jalen Williams left the court on a stretcher after his left leg gave way and appeared seriously injured.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Australia beat Fiji 36-22 to reach Rugby League World Cup semi-finals
content: Defending champions Australia overcame a late challenge to defeat Fiji 36‑22 in their second pool match of the Rugby League World Cup. The win secured Australia’s semi‑final berth with one pool game remaining.
summary: Australia, the defending champions, came from behind to defeat Fiji 36-22 in their second pool match of the Rugby League World Cup. The win secured Australia a semi-final berth with one pool game remaining.
author: BBC Sport

title: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff says Kimi Antonelli's Austin win was his best yet
content: Kimi Antonelli's Austin win was "the best he has delivered", according to Mercedes boss Toto Wolff, even if it wasn't quite enough to give him the title.
summary: Kimi Antonelli won the race in Austin. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said it was the best Antonelli has delivered but not enough to give him the title.
author: BBC Sport

title: Michigan Senate candidate El‑Sayed says Trump respects Constitution like toilet paper
content: Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed criticized President Trump on Sunday, saying the president has as much regard for the Constitution as “a piece of toilet paper.” In an interview with Al Sharpton on PoliticsNation, El-Sayed was asked about the numerous attacks made by the GOP and Trump about his family background and faith and how…
summary: Abdul El‑Sayed, a Michigan Senate candidate, said President Trump has as much regard for the Constitution as “a piece of toilet paper.” He made the comment in a Sunday interview with Al Sharpton on PoliticsNation about GOP attacks on his family background and faith.
author: The Hill

title: Trump says he is considering moving White House press corps from historic location
content: President Trump confirmed on Sunday that he is considering moving the White House press corps from its historic location. In a lengthy Truth Social post that also addressed comedian Bill Maher, he said he is not building a swimming pool in the White House Briefing Room and never intended to do so.
summary: President Trump confirmed on Sunday he is considering moving the White House press corps from its historic location. He also posted on Truth Social that he is not building a swimming pool in the White House Briefing Room, referencing comedian Bill Maher.
author: The Hill

title: Nicki Minaj promises support to President Trump at rally
content: Nicki Minaj joined President Trump at a Sunday campaign rally, stating she would support him if he decides to run for office again. During her appearance, Minaj declared it an honor to stand with the President and affirmed her intention to continue supporting him indefinitely.
summary: Nicki Minaj joined President Trump at a campaign rally on Sunday. She pledged to support him forever and said she would back him if he runs again.
author: The Hill

title: ER visits and hospitalizations for substance use rise ~5% yearly among mothers with young children
content: A large study published in the Canadian Medical Association Journal found that emergency department visits for substance use—particularly opioids, amphetamines and cannabis—by mothers with dependent children rose by almost 5 percent annually. By contrast, females without children experienced an increase of just under 2 percent per year. The growth was concentrated among mothers younger than 25, whose visit rates increased more than four times faster than those of other women.
summary: ER visits and hospitalizations for substance use rise ~5% yearly among mothers with young children.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Lumina simulation traces universe's exit from dark ages via hydrogen and helium re‑ionization
content: With the Big Bang, the universe burst into existence as a hot and dense soup of electrons and subatomic particles. This primordial ionized plasma, initially smaller than a single atom, rapidly expanded and cooled. In the process, particles in the soup slowed enough to bind with electrons, forming electrically neutral hydrogen. As this neutral hydrogen accumulated, the effect was like a shroud, preventing light and other forms of radiation from freely passing through. Around 380,000 years after the Big Bang, the universe was plunged into a cosmic “dark age.” Now, a new computer simulation is giving scientists a detailed view of how the first galaxies, stars, and other structures could have unfolded from that time, to eventually pull the universe out of its dark age. In a paper appearing today in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS), physicists from MIT, Harvard University, and elsewhere present Lumina — a large-volume, high-resolution simulation that follows the early universe from the dark ages through the next 2 billion years of cosmic evolution. Two pivotal transformations Lumina covers a huge patch of the early universe that spans 500 megaparsecs, or about 1.6 billion light-years wide. In that space, the simulation tracks the evolution of dark matter, gas, stars, and radiation (such as photons), across enormous cosmic scales and also zooming down to the detail of an individual developing galaxy. Over the 2 billion years that Lumina simulates, it captures the emergence of two huge transformations in cosmic history: hydrogen re-ionization and helium re-ionization. Hydrogen re-ionization is a period when early stars were able to push out enough ultraviolet light to interact with neutral hydrogen and strip it of its electron. This “re-ionizing” prevented the hydrogen from absorbing photons, instead allowing light to travel freely. Hydrogen re-ionization helped to lift the veil of neutral hydrogen — a process that Lumina captures in detail for the first time. The simulation also tracks helium re-ionization, a process similar to its hydrogen counterpart, in which much higher-energy light breaks apart neutral helium. In its detailed simulations, Lumina revealed that hydrogen re-ionization was likely driven by light from early galaxies and stars. In contrast, helium re-ionization was fueled by much more energetic early supermassive black holes in their active, accreting phases. Together, this represents the first time a simulation has captured both hydrogen and helium re-ionization. “Lumina does everything from small-scale star and galaxy formation to large-scale re-ionization of hydrogen and helium, in a volume that is 100 times larger than previous best simulations,” says study author Mark Vogelsberger, a professor of physics at MIT. He and his colleagues are making Lumina available to the scientific community so that scientists can compare its detailed simulations of the evolution of early cosmic structures with snapshots taken by new and future telescopes. Then, they might begin to piece together the processes that shaped the first galaxies, stars, and structures in the universe. The study’s MIT co-authors are Xuejian (Jacob) Shen and Teodora-Elena Bluichi. Additional authors include first author Oliver Zier (a former postdoc in the Vogelsberger Lab), Rongrong Liu, Sonja Koehler, and Lars Hernquist of the Harvard and Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics; Aaron Smith of the University of Texas at Dallas; Rahul Kannan of York University in Canada, and Volker Springel and Rüdiger Pakmor of Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics in Germany. Cosmic computation Lumina takes its name from the Latin word meaning “lights.” At the heart of Lumina is IllustrisTNG, which was previously developed by scientists at MIT and elsewhere, including members of the Lumina team. IllustrisTNG is a large-scale simulation that tracks the interactions of dark matter, gas, and other processes involved in forming galaxies, from the Big Bang to the present day. In building Lumina, the team refined IllustrisTNG’s code to enable the simulation to track the formation of galaxies with the same level of detail but throughout a much larger volume. They combined this leveled-up galaxy model with a model of radiation transport, which simulates how different forms of radiation such as ultraviolet light interact at extremely large, cosmic scales to capture processes such as hydrogen re-ionization. The new and improved simulation resolves extremely fine details across huge scales. In practice, the simulation encompasses half a trillion individual elements, including dark matter particles and gas cells, which is about 30 times higher-resolution than IllustrisTNG. Lumina captures all this detail and evolves it forward in time, across an enormous patch of about 500 megaparsecs, which is 100 times larger in volume than previous simulations. Running the calculations for every single cell over 2 billions years of cosmic time, and across extremely large and very small scales, involves a significant amount of computing power. The team ran Lumina on Frontier, one of the world’s most powerful supercomputers, based at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee. “At peak scale, the calculation brings together the equivalent of more than 100,000 CPU cores and around 15,000 GPUs,” says Shen. “Making all of those processors communicate efficiently while continuously evolving trillions of interacting pieces of information is itself an extraordinary feat of computer engineering.” Full zoom Lumina begins its simulations at around 45 million years after the Big Bang, in the midst of the dark ages, when neutral hydrogen dominated the early universe. The researchers set the simulation with initial conditions approximating what physicists theorize should have existed in such a dark cosmic period. They then let Lumina run to calculate how matter at those times, in the form of gas and dark matter, interacts across the simulation’s half-a-trillion cells. Simultaneously, the simulation calculates where and how radiation, such as ultraviolet light from stars, emerges and interacts with its surroundings. On the project website, the team provides a number of videos that depict the various scales, time periods, physical processes, and layers of cosmic structures that Lumina simulates. Examples include a “zoom-in” from the full, large-scale patch of the universe to a single, disk-shaped galaxy; and a time-lapse of the full volume, over 2 billion years, that captures the pattern of hydrogen as it is re-ionized over time. “On the one hand, it’s evolving dark matter as well as the gas in the universe, and on the other, it’s also tracking how radiation travels,” Zier explains. “We see dark matter and gas start to clump in these over-densities. And when we zoom in, we can see gas is falling into these dark matter haloes. Zooming in more, we see this is where the first galaxies form. And the first stars form in those first galaxies. Those stars then create radiation. The simulation then tracks that radiation, and we can zoom way out to see how that radiation travels out from stars, through the universe, until at some point it ionizes some neutral hydrogen.” “Other simulations cannot zoom in as far as this,” Vogelsberger notes. “The difference between the smallest and largest scales that we simulate is larger than in any other simulation.” Looking ahead, the team plans to apply Lumina to map the large-scale structure of the early universe. The simulation can also help to predict the gravitational-wave patterns that early galaxies and black holes might produce. Whatever Lumina simulates could soon be compared with actual observations from new and upcoming telescopes. “One of Lumina's major advantages is its sheer size,” Shen says. “It produces enormous populations of simulated galaxies, finally allowing us to make comparisons with the very large galaxy samples that upcoming surveys will observe.” This research was supported, in part, by NASA and the National Science Foundation, and used resources of the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory, which is supported by the Advanced Scientific Computing Research programs in the Office of Science of the U. S. Department of Energy.
summary: With the Big Bang, the universe burst into existence as a hot and dense soup of electrons and subatomic particles. This primordial ionized plasma, initially smaller than a single atom, rapidly expanded and cooled.
author: MIT News

title: Scientists achieve 99.9% accuracy operating five silicon qubits simultaneously
content: Scientists have demonstrated a method to run multiple silicon qubits at the same time with high precision, addressing a key hurdle for scaling quantum computers. The technique kept an accuracy of about 99.9 percent even when all five qubits operated concurrently, suggesting a path toward larger, more powerful quantum processors.
summary: Scientists discovered a method to run multiple silicon qubits at once with high precision. The technique maintained roughly 99.9% accuracy when all five qubits operated together, addressing a major scaling challenge.
author: Science Daily

title: Simple liquid paint stops cavities in children, major trial shows
content: A major clinical trial involving young children found that a simple liquid painted onto teeth in seconds can stop cavities without drilling, injections or anesthesia. The inexpensive treatment could spare thousands of children painful dental procedures and surgery and may lead to broader FDA‑approved use.
summary: The liquid can be painted onto teeth in seconds and stops cavities without drilling, injections, or anesthesia, according to a major clinical trial involving young children. The inexpensive treatment could spare thousands of children painful dental procedures and may lead to broader FDA‑approved use.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA PACE satellite maps fall foliage redness shift southward in early Oct 2026
content:
NASA’s Earth Observatory has released a series of global maps that chart the spread of autumn “redness” across the planet, using data from the Ocean Color Instrument (OCI) aboard the PACE satellite. The maps cover two one‑week periods: September 29 – October 4 and October 5 – 11, 2026. In the first week, the most intense red vegetation appears in Alaska, northern Canada, Mongolia, and Russia, with smaller patches in Australia. By the second week the reddest areas have moved equatorward, showing increased color in the Mid‑Atlantic, the U.S. Southeast, southern Russia, China, and Mongolia.

The OCI collects data in 286 spectral bands, including wavelengths that detect anthocyanins, carotenoids, and chlorophylls—pigments that change as leaves transition from green to yellow, orange, and red. NASA scientists compare the ratio of red to green reflectance over time to determine where leaves are changing and when color peaks. The maps use a color scale from dark green (values near 1, indicating equal red and green) to light yellow and red, which represent progressively higher levels of red pigment relative to green.

In New England and upstate New York, the maps show redness fading during the week of October 5 – 11, even as the Midwest and Mid‑Atlantic spread the color. The satellite also detects high redness in agricultural regions of Brazil, Australia, and Canada, where crop anthocyanin levels can mimic fall foliage. Cloud cover can create gaps in the vegetation signal.

The Earth Observatory article highlights the role of the Global Learning and Observations to Benefit the Environment (GLOBE) program’s North American Phenology Campaign. NASA data scientist Skye Caplan has been posting weekly foliage maps and is asking the public to submit ground photographs to help “ground truth” the satellite observations. These images can refine PACE’s measurements and support research on spring greening, fall senescence, the global carbon cycle, wildfire risk, and early warning signs of drought, insect infestations, and plant disease.

The article also notes that the PACE satellite is the first to measure all three key leaf pigments—anthocyanins, carotenoids, and chlorophylls—across the entire planet every day or two. This capability, according to vegetation scientist Karl Huemmrich of the University of Maryland, Baltimore County, is “game‑changing” because it provides time‑series data that reveal peak redness and yellowness anywhere on Earth.
summary: NASA PACE satellite maps fall foliage redness shift southward in early Oct 2026.
author: NASA News

title: APOD Highlights M42 Great Nebula in Orion on Oct. 26, 2026
content: APOD Science APOD 2026 October 26 – M42: The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. M42: The Great Nebula in Orion Explanation: The Great Nebula in Orion, an immense, nearby starbirth region, is one the most famous of all astronomical nebulas. Here, glowing gas surrounds hot young stars at the edge of an immense interstellar molecular cloud only 1500 light-years away. In the featured deep image in assigned colors highlighted by emission in hydrogen, wisps and sheets of dust and gas are particularly evident. The Great Nebula in Orion can be found with the unaided eye near the easily identifiable belt of three stars in the popular constellation Orion. In addition to housing a bright open cluster of stars known as the Trapezium, the Orion Nebula contains many stellar nurseries. These nurseries contain much hydrogen gas, hot young stars, proplyds, and stellar jets spewing material at high speeds. Also known as M42, the Orion Nebula spans about 40 light years and is located in the same spiral arm of our Galaxy as the Sun. Tomorrow’s picture: open space Date: October 26, 2026 Credit & Copyright: Roberto Palaia Authors & editors: Robert Nemiroff, Jerry Bonnell, Cecilia Chirenti, Keighley Rockcliffe A service of: ASD at NASA / GSFC, NASA Science Activation & Michigan Tech. U. Random APOD Generator Yesterday’s Image APOD: 2026 October 25 – Dark Matter in a Simulated Universe Tomorrow’s Image
summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day for October 26, 2026 featured a deep color image of M42, the Great Nebula in Orion. The nebula is a nearby star‑birth region about 1,500 light‑years away, spans roughly 40 light‑years, and contains the Trapezium star cluster and many stellar nurseries.
author: NASA News

title: Lula wins Brazil presidential election as Bolsonaro refuses to accept results
content: Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured the presidential election, while incumbent Jair Bolsonaro has refused to accept the outcome. Lula’s win diverges from a recent regional pattern of right‑of‑center candidates linked to former U.S. President Donald Trump, and suggests that the continent’s largest economy may keep resisting Trump’s demands despite heightened tariff pressures.
summary: Lula's victory runs counter to a regional trend of wins for right‑of‑center candidates aligned with Trump. The result suggests Brazil, Latin America’s largest economy, will likely keep defying Trump’s demands despite pressure from higher tariffs.
author: Euronews

title: UN aviation agency proposes plan to curb circling delays and cut emissions
content: Air traffic delays are described as costing billions and turning journeys into ordeals. The content notes that several countries have demonstrated that improved coordination can save thousands of flying hours and reduce emissions. The United Nations’ aviation agency is urging other nations to adopt similar coordination measures.
summary: Air traffic delays that make planes circle before landing cost billions and turn journeys into ordeals. The UN’s aviation agency urges worldwide adoption of a coordination plan that some countries have shown can save thousands of flying hours and cut emissions.
author: UN News

title: Young Buyers Make Up 55% of Monzo Payments for Bayeux Tapestry Tickets
content:
A 1,000-year-old embroidery has emerged as a pop culture sensation, with young people reportedly preferring tickets to the Bayeux tapestry over Hollywood blockbusters. Data from Monzo indicates that in the first hour of the second ticket release last Wednesday, payments to the British Museum reached £14,100, which was 48 times higher than a typical Wednesday morning.

The surge was driven largely by younger demographics, with 55% of the cardholders making these payments aged under 35. This trend highlights a significant shift in consumer interest, as the historical artifact attracted more immediate financial commitment from a young audience than current film releases.
summary: In the first hour of the second round of tickets for the Bayeux tapestry at the British Museum, Monzo cardholder payments reached £14,100, 48 times a normal Wednesday morning. More than half (55%) of those purchasers were under 35 years old.
author: Guardian World

title: Employers warn higher apprenticeship costs for over‑25s could hurt youth jobs plan
content:
Britain’s ministers are preparing to revise the apprenticeship funding system so that training a worker aged over 25 in England will cost 25 percent more than it does now, according to the Guardian. The change is intended to steer firms toward employing younger people.

The Guardian reports that the country’s largest employers have warned the government that the higher cost for older‑worker training could undermine the policy’s aim of addressing the youth jobs crisis.
summary: Ministers plan to overhaul Labour’s apprenticeship funding scheme to raise the cost of training workers over the age of 25 in England by 25%. Britain’s largest employers say the higher cost could damage the government’s goal to tackle the youth jobs crisis.
author: Guardian World

title: Covert prison recording of Beau Lamarre-Condon apology played at double murder trial
content:
A covert recording captured former police officer Beau Lamarre‑Condon during a prison meeting in December last year. In the clip he told a friend, “I fully take accountability that you’re involved because of me now,” and the statement was heard by a Sydney court. Lamarre‑Condon, 31, has apologized to the friend, acknowledging that the friend’s involvement stems from his actions.

The court case concerns Lamarre‑Condon’s alleged use of his police service weapon to fatally shoot Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024. The officer is charged with double murder in the incident.
summary: A covert recording captured Beau Lamarre-Condon telling a friend in a December prison meeting that he fully takes accountability because the friend is involved because of him. Lamarre-Condon, 31, is accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
author: Guardian World

title: Victorian coroner may refer birthkeeper Emily Lal for alleged hospital‑fear grooming
content:
A Victorian coroner has heard that birthkeeper Emily Lal allegedly “groomed” pregnant women to fear hospital birth.  In the case of Stacey Warnecke, Lal reportedly told her that Warnecke’s “condition and mindset” needed to be “solid” to avoid giving birth in a hospital.  

Warnecke died in September 2025 at Frankston Hospital after giving birth at home and suffering a postpartum haemorrhage, with Lal by her side.  She had paid Lal $6,000 to support her throughout her pregnancy.  The coroner may refer Lal to prosecutors for potential criminal charges.
summary: Victorian coroner may refer birthkeeper Emily Lal for alleged hospital‑fear grooming.
author: Guardian World

title: Former RAAF pilot Robert John Crawford pleads not guilty to wife's murder
content: A jury heard that former RAAF pilot Robert John Crawford, 49, was described as a “love rat” and “master manipulator” who allegedly staged his wife’s death to look like an accident. Crawford is on trial after the body of his wife, Frances Elizabeth Crawford, was found near a ride‑on lawnmower on their Toowoomba property. The alleged murder is said to have occurred at Upper Lockyer on 29 July 2024, and Crawford entered a not‑guilty plea on Monday.
summary: Former RAAF pilot Robert John Crawford pleads not guilty to wife's murder.
author: Guardian World

title: Angus Taylor criticised for tone‑deaf response to alleged attack on Helen Haines
content: Zali Steggall and Monique Ryan say Coalition leader was wrong to deny link between parliamentary debate and political violence Angus Taylor has been criticised for his response to the alleged attack on Helen Haines, with crossbenchers Monique Ryan and Zali Steggall labelling a speech by the opposition leader “tone deaf” and saying he did not “read the room”. Parliament returned in Canberra on Monday, a week after an alleged attack outside the Indi MP’s northern Victorian electorate office, which led to her losing both legs. A 43-year-old man has been charged and the incident continues to be investigated.
summary: Angus Taylor criticised for tone‑deaf response to alleged attack on Helen Haines.
author: Guardian World

title: Lula wins fourth nonconsecutive term, defeating far‑right senator Flávio Bolsonaro
content:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a fourth non‑consecutive term as Brazil’s president, defeating far‑right senator Flávio Bolsonaro in a closely contested vote. The victory marks a reversal for Lula against his opponent, who is identified as the leader of a radical populist movement associated with his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. Jair Bolsonaro is currently serving a 27‑year prison sentence for plotting a coup after his loss in the 2022 election.

The newsletter notes that Lula’s win will be examined for its potential impact on Brazil’s democratic institutions, environmental policies, and international relations. It highlights the contrast between Lula’s left‑leaning platform and the far‑right stance of his opponent, suggesting a shift in Brazil’s political direction.

In addition to the Brazilian election, the newsletter references other global headlines, including a student‑led movement in Serbia that removed long‑serving leader Aleksandar Vučić, severe weather impacts in the United Kingdom, and various political developments in Europe and North America. These items are presented alongside the Brazilian story as part of a broader daily briefing.
summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a fourth nonconsecutive term as Brazil’s president, beating far‑right senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27‑year prison sentence for plotting a coup.
author: Guardian World

title: Labour urged to address projected £400m overseas aid shortfall by 2027
content:
The UK is projected to miss its target of spending 0.3% of national income on international aid by an estimated £400 million by the end of 2027. Calculations from the Center for Global Development indicate that official development assistance funding is on course for a significant shortfall below this promised level.

Consequently, Labour has been urged to address the predicted gap in overseas aid funding. The official forecast highlights that the country is not currently on track to meet its financial commitments for international development support in the coming years.
summary: Official forecasts show the UK is on track to miss its 0.3% of national income target for official development assistance by about £400 million by the end of next year. The Center for Global Development calculated the shortfall will remain at the end of 2027, prompting calls for Labour to plug the gap.
author: Guardian World

title: Rapper Nicki Minaj appears onstage with Trump at Michigan rally
content: Rapper Nicki Minaj, the “Super Bass” singer, joined former President Donald Trump onstage at a rally in Michigan. She is the latest big‑name figure to campaign in the state, where a tight Senate race is unfolding ahead of the 3 November midterm elections.
summary: The Super Bass singer is the latest big name to campaign in Michigan. A tight Senate race is playing out there ahead of the 3 November midterms.
author: BBC World

title: Birmingham secure first WSL win with 1-0 victory over Charlton
content: Wilda Leidhammar scored the only goal as Birmingham secured their first Women's Super League win of the season, defeating bottom‑placed Charlton 1‑0. The match took place at St Andrew’s, while Charlton remain without a point in the competition.
summary: Wilda Leidhammar scored the only goal in Birmingham's 1-0 win over Charlton. The match took place at St Andrew's, giving Birmingham their first WSL victory of the season.
author: BBC Sport

title: Jake Jarman wins historic second silver at World Gymnastics Championships
content: Jake Jarman has become the first British male gymnast to win two individual medals at the same World Gymnastics Championships. He claimed silver in the vault final, adding a historic second podium finish to his achievements at the event.
summary: Jake Jarman became the first British male gymnast to win two individual medals at the same World Gymnastics Championships. He claimed silver in the vault final.
author: BBC Sport

title: Manchester City’s Women’s WSL Perfect Start Ends in 1-1 Draw with Manchester United
content:
Manchester City had a perfect record in the Women’s Super League.

The streak ended when the team drew 1‑1 with rivals Manchester United, after Elisabeth Terland scored a late equaliser.
summary: Manchester City’s Women’s team lost their perfect start in the Women's Super League after a 1-1 draw with Manchester United. Elisabeth Terland scored a late equaliser for United.
author: BBC Sport

title: Alderweireld blames lack of togetherness for United's 3-0 loss to Bournemouth
content: Match of the Day pundits Toby Alderweireld and Ashley Williams analyse Manchester United's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth, with Alderweireld suggesting there is no "togetherness" amongst the United squad.
summary: Match of the Day pundits Toby Alderweireld and Ashley Williams analyse Manchester United's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth. Alderweireld suggests there is no "togetherness" amongst the United squad.
author: BBC Sport

title: New Act Seeks to Keep Film and TV Production in the U.S.
content: The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act has been introduced to address the growing trend of film and television production relocating abroad. The Act proposes a federal tax incentive aimed at encouraging producers to keep projects within the United States.
summary: The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act has been introduced. It proposes a federal tax incentive to counter the trend of film and television production moving overseas.
author: The Hill

title: Sen. Thom Tillis says it's appropriate to review Alaska Senate race with two Dan Sullivans
content: Sen. Thom Tillis (R‑NC) said on Sunday that it was “appropriate to take a look at” the outcome of the Alaska Senate race because two candidates on the ballot share similar names. His remarks prompted a lawsuit from the Department of Justice. Tillis added that Alaska has a candidate who “just coincidentally happens to be the same name as my friend.”
summary: Sen. Thom Tillis says it's appropriate to review Alaska Senate race with two Dan Sullivans.
author: The Hill

title: Experienced teachers quitting or cutting hours amid global shortages
content:
Teacher shortages are affecting school systems worldwide, prompting governments to launch initiatives that aim to attract new graduates into teaching.  

While the focus has largely been on boosting supply, little attention has been given to why experienced teachers are quitting or cutting hours, despite the significant costs of turnover—including recruitment, training, and lost continuity.
summary: Teacher shortages are affecting school systems in countries across the world. Governments have responded with initiatives to attract graduates into teaching, but far less attention has been paid to why experienced teachers are quitting or reducing hours despite the high costs of turnover.
author: Phys.org

title: Lumina simulation reveals early universe on record-breaking scale
content:
The James Webb Space Telescope and Nancy Roman Space Telescope are providing unprecedented detail on the universe’s earliest chapters.  

In response, researchers at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian have created “Lumina,” described as one of the largest and most detailed simulations ever produced of the early universe.
summary: Researchers at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian developed the "Lumina" simulation, one of the largest and most detailed models of the early universe. The simulation helps astronomers interpret data from the James Webb Space Telescope and Nancy Roman Space Telescope.
author: Phys.org

title: Best apps for tracking reading and discovering new books
content: The article notes that many apps claim to help users track their reading and discover new books. It has compiled a list of some of the best options to assist readers in choosing the right app for their needs.
summary: There are numerous apps on the market that promise to track reading and suggest new books. A compiled list highlights some of the best options to help users pick the right one.
author: TechCrunch

title: Data centre debate intensifies before US midterms amid environmental concerns
content: The discussion around data centres is intensifying as the US midterm elections approach. While data centres are described as the lifeblood of the digital world, concerns are mounting over their environmental impact. The BBC is examining the growth of data centres through charts.
summary: Data centres are described as the lifeblood of the digital world, but concerns about their environmental impact are growing. The BBC examines the sector’s growth using charts.
author: BBC Technology

title: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva wins fourth term over Flavio Bolsonaro
content: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, nearly 81, secured a fourth term after a runoff on Sunday, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro. Official results gave Lula 51.7 percent of the vote and Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, 48.2 percent.
summary: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva wins fourth term over Flavio Bolsonaro.
author: France 24

title: Lula faces divided Brazil, hostile Congress, weak finances and Trump‑like threat in fourth term
content: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva will have to wrestle with a divided Brazil, an unfriendly Congress, feeble public finances and a Donald Trump-shaped menace during his unprecedented fourth term.
summary: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is beginning an unprecedented fourth term. He will have to wrestle with a divided Brazil, an unfriendly Congress, feeble public finances and a Donald Trump‑shaped menace.
author: France 24

title: Victorian emergency services minister Paul Edbrooke finds bullet with 'RAT' etched on his car
content:
Victoria’s emergency services minister, Paul Edbrooke, said he fears for his family’s safety after a bullet was left on his car on Saturday. The bullet was etched with the word “RAT” and his former firefighter number, and was discovered on the bonnet when he returned to the vehicle after speaking with community members.

Edbrooke’s concerns come amid heightened worries for MPs following an alleged attack on fellow Labor member Helen Haines. The incident was first reported by the Herald Sun on Monday.
summary: Paul Edbrooke said he fears for his family’s safety after a bullet bearing the word “RAT” and his former firefighter number was left on his car’s bonnet on Saturday. The Herald Sun reported on Monday that he discovered the bullet after speaking with community members.
author: Guardian World

title: PM Albanese leads parliament pause to honor Indi MP Helen Haines after attack
content:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese led parliamentary tributes to independent MP Helen Haines on Monday, describing her as “a fighter” with a deep love of her community. The House paused for speeches about Haines, her husband Phil and her staff while she remained in a serious but stable condition at Melbourne’s Alfred Hospital, a week after she was allegedly targeted in an attack outside her electorate office.

Separately, Liberal MP Angus Taylor and National MP Barnaby Joyce rejected recent calls to change parliamentary practice aimed at cooling political debate.
summary: PM Albanese leads parliament pause to honor Indi MP Helen Haines after attack.
author: Guardian World

title: Commonwealth ombudsman says government aged‑care algorithm is unreasonable, unfair
content: Report from commonwealth ombudsman finds ‘technological black box’ ignores transparency recommendations from robodebt royal commission Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast An algorithm used by the federal government to assess the level of care older Australians are entitled to is unreasonable, unfair and lacks human oversight, according to a damning investigation by the commonwealth ombudsman. The investigation also found transparency recommendations from the robodebt royal commission have been ignored. Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
summary: The commonwealth ombudsman found the federal government's algorithm for assessing aged care entitlements is unreasonable, unfair and lacks human oversight. The investigation also said transparency recommendations from the robodebt royal commission have been ignored.
author: Guardian World

title: Xi's anti-corruption drive highlighted ahead of China's top leaders meeting
content:
China’s upcoming fifth plenum of top leaders is drawing attention to President Xi Jinping’s long‑running anti‑corruption campaign. Since assuming power in 2012, Xi pledged to eradicate corruption throughout the Communist Party, and the pace of investigations has continued unabated.  

Chinese disciplinary authorities opened investigations last year into more than one million individuals, a count that included over one hundred officials at ministerial or provincial level. Analysts note that the sheer scale of the purges has sparked debate over whether the driving concern is corruption itself or a perceived lack of loyalty among cadres.  

As the plenary session convenes, party discipline and loyalty are reported to be prominent items on the agenda, reflecting the heightened focus on maintaining strict internal control within the Chinese Communist Party.
summary: Chinese Communist Party officials are preparing for an important meeting this week with discipline and party loyalty high on the agenda. Last year disciplinary authorities opened investigations into more than 1 million people, including over 100 officials at ministerial or provincial level, as Xi Jinping’s anti‑corruption campaign continues a decade after his 2012 pledge.
author: Guardian World

title: Lula secures fourth term, beating Flávio Bolsonaro with 51.75% of vote
content: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a fourth term as Brazil’s president, defeating far‑right challenger Flávio Bolsonaro in a comeback after narrowly losing the first round. With nearly 99 % of votes counted, the 80‑year‑old incumbent received 51.75 % of the vote, while the 45‑year‑old Bolsonaro obtained 48.25 %. The result marks an unprecedented reversal for the leftist incumbent, who reclaimed the presidency in what the source describes as a historic upset.
summary: Lula secures fourth term, beating Flávio Bolsonaro with 51.75% of vote.
author: Guardian World

title: Bill Murray stars in new golf documentary A Course Called Ireland
content:
A new documentary titled A Course Called Ireland features Bill Murray golfing across the "Emerald Isle" while reflecting on subjects ranging from his great-grandmother to worms. The film is described as a travelogue in which the 76-year-old actor appears notably grumpy, with the narrative suggesting he may have wished he were not there. The production includes scenes of sulky car journeys and strained encounters, creating an overall sense of a television series imploding.

The review highlights specific moments from the show, including Murray teeing off in County Kerry and observing "hardworking Irish worms" in coastal Cork. It also notes instances where the actor says "hah-hah" in various golf-adjacent locations, surrounded by locals whose body language implies they are similarly reacting. Despite the initial excitement of seeing the star known for his roles in Groundhog Day and Lost in Translation, the tone of the documentary is characterized by a lack of the bittersweet humor anticipated by viewers.
summary: The new documentary features Bill Murray golfing around Ireland while reflecting on his great-grandmother and worms. The review describes the actor as grumpy and notes that the series feels like it is imploding.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Mbappé double gives Real Madrid late win at Barcelona after Raphinha equaliser
content: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou, and he led them out again with a late, late victory that opens up a whole new world. With three minutes remaining and the energy with which they had played dropping, a wonderful piece of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run on a night in which there were so many of them. Camavinga sprinted into the area, slipped away from Pau Cubarsí and pulled the ball back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and Madrid had won it, Mbappé getting his second goal of a special match to end Barcelona’s record nine-game winning run.
