So much for a battering, so much for Barcelona going nine points clear, the title race run before November; there is life in Madrid and in this league. Life in their manager too; this was planned and executed to perfection, and not the way that might have been expected.
summary: José Mourinho’s Real Madrid secured a late victory at Camp Nou with Kylian Mbappé’s second goal of the match. The win ended Barcelona’s record nine‑game winning run that had left them nine points clear in the title race.

title: Kimi Antonelli wins US F1 GP, set to become youngest champion in Mexico
content:

The 20-year-old championship leader delivered a composed drive that, according to Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff, represents a significant step toward securing the Formula One world title.

Although Antonelli could not clinch the championship during the race in Texas, the result has made his title defense a near formality. He is expected to officially become the youngest F1 champion at the next round in Mexico, with the coronation now seemingly only a week away.
summary: Kimi Antonelli secured a dominant victory at the US Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen. The 20-year-old championship leader is expected to officially seal the title at the next round in Mexico.

title: Scott Walker's 2006 album The Drift explores death and tragedy
content: In my mind, Spooky Season music comes in two distinct flavors. There are the fun, occasionally goofy songs like "The Monster Mash" and John Carpenter's "Halloween Theme." Then there is the genuinely terrifying: Throbbing Gristle, The Body, or Scott Walker's The Drift. This 2006 album from the singer-songwriter is truly upsetting. On it, Walker explores death, disease, and tragedy. But not just from some abstract perspective. There are visceral descriptions of the hanging of Benito Mussolini and his mistress Clara Petacci. He sings about 9/11, his stillborn twin brother, and the Srebrenica genocide. Lyrically, it's about as dark as an album …
summary: The Drift is a 2006 album by singer‑songwriter Scott Walker that delves into themes of death, disease and tragedy. Its lyrics include visceral references to the hanging of Benito Mussolini and Clara Petacci, the 9/11 attacks, Walker’s stillborn twin brother, and the Srebrenica genocide.

summary: iFixit opened the iPhone Duo and gave it a 5/10 repairability score, the highest the site has awarded to a foldable yet. content:
Ballot counting has resumed in Brazil after a two‑hour voting extension ordered by the Supreme Court on Sunday. The extension came as presidential candidate Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and senator Flávio Bolsonaro await the final results.

The local electoral court also ordered the immediate restoration of the entire municipal bus fleet and issued an arrest warrant for municipal transport secretary Pablo Souza on suspicion of an electoral offence and for disobeying court orders. The warrant could not be executed because Souza is in Paris on an “official mission” and is not expected to return to Brazil until Monday.

title: Possible Roberts Road Expansion as SpaceX pushes for Flight 16
content:
SpaceX is preparing to launch Starship Flight 16 from Launch Complex 39A (LC-39A) at Kennedy Space Center as soon as possible, a move that requires the completion of infrastructure at the Roberts Road campus. The company has applied to expand its Roberts Road footprint from 167 acres to nearly 400 acres in conjunction with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). This expansion, currently in the Draft Programmatic Environmental Assessment (PEA) stage, would allow SpaceX to construct additional Gigabays, a Payload Processing Facility (PPF), Project Ignition ship static-fire stands, and a new road connecting Roberts Road to NASA Parkway. The PEA will undergo a public comment period before final approvals are granted.

The Roberts Road site has evolved significantly since 2021, when SpaceX began using it to store and refurbish Falcon 9 boosters. While initial plans included building Mega Bays for Starship production, those specific structures were canceled as focus shifted to Starbase, Texas. The steel intended for the first Roberts Road Mega Bay was instead used to construct Mega Bay 2 at Starbase. The site now houses Hangar X-2, which processes Dragon spacecraft and Starlink payloads, and a facility for baking Starship tiles. In January 2025, SpaceX secured an extension to the north of Hangar X to begin Starship operations, resulting in the construction of the first Gigabay and the installation of a transfer-aisle bridge crane.

At LC-39A, SpaceX has completed the addition of two Liquid Methane (LCH4) storage tanks, bringing the site’s capacity to nearly 5,000 metric tons of LCH4, sufficient for approximately 3.8 launch stacks. The company also increased Liquid Nitrogen capacity for the deluge farm and installed a reinforced roof on the tower in October 2024 to protect against ship catches. With all four stacked towers now featuring reinforced roofs, SpaceX has initiated activation testing of pad systems, including the tower vent in September 2024 and the top-deck deluge system in late September 2024.

Ship 43 completed cryo-proof testing in October 2024 and is scheduled to roll back to Mega Bay 2 for engine installation and final assembly. Because SpaceX lacks ship-testing capabilities at Kennedy Space Center, Ship 43 must complete static fire testing at Starbase before transport. Based on previous timelines, the ship is expected to be ready for static fire in mid-December 2024 and could be transported to Kennedy Space Center in early to mid-January 2025. It is anticipated to arrive missing only its payload and Flight Termination System charges.

Booster 23 completed cryo-proof testing in October 2024 and is slated for static fire testing at LC-39A in late November 2024. This booster test will further activate the pad systems. A full-stack wet dress rehearsal, involving both Booster 23 and Ship 43, could occur in mid-December 2024, potentially leading to the first Starship flight from LC-39A in late January 2025. Meanwhile, construction continues at SLC-37A, where two storage tanks are already in place, though the site is not expected to be operational for at least another year.
summary: Possible Roberts Road Expansion as SpaceX pushes for Flight 16.
author: NASASpaceFlight

title: Hull Maintains Unbeaten Home Record After Draw With Brentford
content:
Hull’s home record remains unbeaten after a draw with Brentford, though the Tigers have gone seven games without a win.

summary: Hull’s unbeaten home record remains intact but the Tigers have not tasted victory for seven games after this draw with Brentford. The opening goal came courtesy of a 24th‑minute Oli McBurnie penalty, awarded when Aaron Hickey flattened Tim Iroegbunam while trying to hook the ball away.

title: Osula and Barnes score as Newcastle beat Palace, pressuring manager Pierre Sage
content: The first half was dreadful. The pass completion rate was a meagre 72.8%, although it felt lower. There were only two shots on target. The sun kept popping out from behind the clouds to take a look, and then going back in again, appalled. And the really bad news for Crystal Palace is that, for them, that was the good bit. Newcastle were much improved after the break. Will Osula touched in a Jacob Murphy cross two minutes after half-time, Joe Willock had an effort ruled out for a marginal offside five minutes later, and Harvey Barnes completed a slick passing move six minutes after that. A smattering of boos from the home fans made clear what everybody already knew. Quarter of an hour of proper football had been enough to win the game, and that leaves Pierre Sage under significant pressure.
summary: Newcastle turned around a dreadful first half to win, with Will Osula scoring from a Jacob Murphy cross two minutes after half-time. Harvey Barnes added a goal six minutes later, leaving Palace manager Pierre Sage under significant pressure.

title: NFL roundup: Falcons spoil Niners’ undefeated start; Steelers win in Paris
content:
The Atlanta Falcons ended the San Francisco 49ers’ undefeated season with a 29-20 victory, snapping a two-game losing streak in the process. Michael Penix Jr. led the offense with three touchdown passes to Nick Muse, Kyle Pitts, and Drake London. The Falcons also capitalized on defensive opportunities, scoring 13 points on four turnovers. The 49ers’ offensive struggles were compounded by injuries and defensive plays; running back Christian McCaffrey missed much of the first half with a thigh injury, while quarterback Brock Purdy threw two interceptions. One of those interceptions was picked off by rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels, who also recovered a fumble by George Kittle.

In other NFL action, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers defeated the Carolina Panthers in a game marking Baker Mayfield’s return to the lineup. The New York Jets improved their record to 5-2 with a late-season victory over the Tennessee Titans. Additionally, the New York Jets handed the Miami Dolphins their first win of the season. The roundup also notes that the Pittsburgh Steelers secured a victory in Paris.
summary: NFL roundup: Falcons spoil Niners’ undefeated start; Steelers win in Paris.

title: Manchester United Board Holds Crisis Talks Over Carrick's Future After 3-0 Defeat
content:
Manchester United’s board is holding crisis discussions regarding Michael Carrick’s future as head coach following a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday. The loss has left the manager’s position in doubt, prompting urgent talks within the club’s hierarchy about whether to dismiss him.

Meanwhile, director of football Jason Wilcox has identified Eddie Howe as his top candidate for the role. Despite the mounting pressure, Carrick remained defiant after the match, stating he was not expecting to be removed from his post. “I totally understand the situation,” Carrick said. “I’m not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. Carrying on as normal, and I love this place.”
summary: Manchester United's hierarchy is holding crisis talks about whether to sack head coach Michael Carrick after a 3-0 loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Carrick, who is defiant, said he is not expecting to be removed and will continue to work normally.

title: Democrats attack Republicans over nearly $1 trillion Medicaid cuts in One Big Beautiful Bill
content:
Democrats in battleground districts are pressuring Republicans over Medicaid cuts in the One Big Beautiful Bill law.  

In campaign ads and on debate stages, Democrats criticize Republicans for supporting a law that will reduce Medicaid funding by nearly $1 trillion to pay for tax cuts primarily.
summary: Democrats in battleground districts are criticizing Republicans for supporting the One Big Beautiful Bill law, which reduces Medicaid funding by nearly $1 trillion. The law uses these savings to pay for tax cuts, a point Democrats are emphasizing in advertisements and debates.
author: The Hill

title: New animal model offers more precise way to study calorie-burning brown fat
content: Researchers at LSU's Pennington Biomedical Research Center have developed and validated a new genetic animal model to study brown and beige fat. These specialized tissues use energy to produce heat and play an important role in metabolism. The findings are published in the journal Scientific Reports.
summary: Researchers at LSU's Pennington Biomedical Research Center have developed and validated a new genetic animal model that gives scientists a more precise way to study brown and beige fat, specialized tissues that use energy to produce heat and play an important role in metabolism. The paper is published in the journal Scientific Reports.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Milky Way's Disk Grew 'Upside Down' With Younger Stars in Thinner Layers
content: The Milky Way contains hundreds of billions of stars arranged in a spiral pattern. Beyond this structure, the galaxy is physically divided into three distinct components: a galactic bulge, a galactic disk, and a galactic halo.
summary: The Milky Way’s disk grew 'upside down,' with younger stars forming in increasingly thinner layers. The galaxy contains hundreds of billions of stars arranged in a spiral pattern and is divided into a bulge, disk, and halo.
author: Phys.org

title: Monarch Butterfly Uses Lightweight Radio-Pulse Tag to Check In via Cellphone
content: New technology has reduced the weight of radio-pulse tags to less than half a gram (0.02 ounces), enabling monarch butterflies to carry them. This development allows the insects to effectively "borrow" a cellphone to check in with people they encounter during their journeys.
summary: Monarch Butterfly Uses Lightweight Radio-Pulse Tag to Check In via Cellphone.
author: Phys.org

title: Crows decide twice as fast as humans and monkeys in visual choice test
content: University of Tübingen researchers demonstrated that crows make visual decisions twice as fast as humans and monkeys. In the study, two carrion crows averaged 235 milliseconds to identify the movement direction of a dot pattern and indicate their choice, while maintaining high accuracy.
summary: University of Tübingen researchers found that carrion crows made a visual choice decision twice as fast as humans and monkeys. In the experiment, the two crows took an average of 235 milliseconds to identify the direction of a dot pattern and indicate their choice while maintaining high accuracy.
author: Phys.org

title: Supercurrent allows non‑destructive reading of quantum information
content: A fundamental challenge in quantum computing is extracting information from a qubit without altering its state. Unlike conventional bits, which can be read repeatedly, direct measurement of a quantum system typically causes the state to collapse before it can be determined, meaning the act of reading modifies the information.
summary: Quantum computing faces the challenge that measuring a qubit collapses its state, altering the information. A supercurrent can read quantum information without destroying it.
author: Phys.org

title: Australian coral reefs face collapse risk by 2075 due to projected ocean warming
content: A global assessment indicates that every shallow-water coral reef ecosystem in Australia faces an extremely high risk of collapse by 2075. The report attributes this potential loss largely to projected ocean warming, warning that drastic action is required to prevent the collapse.
summary: Every shallow‑water coral reef ecosystem in Australia faces an extremely high risk of collapse by 2075. The risk is driven largely by projected ocean warming, according to a global assessment.
author: Phys.org

title: Hurston-1 open source TTS model excels in Southern American and Afro-English accents
content:
Show HN: Hurston‑1 open source TTS that speak Southern American and Afro‑English

A developer has announced the open‑source release of the Hurston‑1 narrowband text‑to‑speech (TTS) model under the Apache‑2.0 license. The model is noted for its strong performance with American English, especially Southern American and Regional African English accents. The creator, who works with Destined AI in Atlanta, said the project was motivated by a fascination with what AI can achieve and a desire to make AI more accessible.

Since 2021 the author has gathered fully consented voice data from over 20,000 people, comprising 1 million audio recordings and more than 1,800 hours of audio. For Hurston‑1, a subset of 136 hours was used to finetune the Maya1 model and expand its capabilities. The narrowband design focuses on telephone‑grade output, a format that the author notes is still widely used for voice interactions.

Hurston‑1 has already been deployed for clients such as Amazon and Salesforce, generating more than half‑million dollars in revenue. The release aims to open up similar opportunities for others.

The model does not preserve a consistent voice across prompts and does not support voice cloning, which may limit its use for podcast production. The author is working on a second version with planned improvements.

Interested parties can download the model from Hugging Face, test it, and provide feedback. The post invites collaboration and can be found on Hacker News at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50227330, where it has received 20 points and 7 comments.
summary: Hey HN, I’m open sourcing my Hurston-1 narrowband TTS model (Apache-2.0). It is very good with American English and does especially well with Southern American and Regional African English accents.
author: Hacker News

title: Zen Browser seen as Arc replacement by user
content: Launcher-like pinned tabs, pop-over glance view, and more make Zen my go to browser. | Image: Zen Browser I know many of you are mourning the loss of the Arc browser, and I get it. It felt like the first app in a long time to really offer a new approach to browser design. Atlassian bought the company last year and shifted its focus to developing Dia, its even more AI-focused browser. And soon enough, Arc will officially be no more, leaving dedicated users in a lurch. But I abandoned Arc quite some time ago for the Zen Browser and haven't really missed it. If you're willing to deal with some minor inconveniences, I think you'll find Zen is the Arc replacement you're looking for. Zen unabashedly rips off all the best bits of Arc. Visually, they'r …
summary: Zen Browser is viewed by the author as a replacement for the soon‑to‑be discontinued Arc browser. The author notes that Atlassian bought Arc last year, shifted focus to Dia, and that Arc will officially be no more, but they have not missed Arc after switching to Zen.
author: The Verge

title: YouTuber CuriousHagi Dissects iPhone Duo, Points to Hinge as Crackgate Source
content:
Reports on social media and the iPhone Duo subreddit describe the foldable phone failing quickly and spectacularly. Some users say they had the device for only a few hours before the hinge caught on something, producing an audible crack that broke the screen. Notably, the cracks appear to occur in the same spot each time.

YouTuber CuriousHagi replicated the cracked screen during durability testing of the iPhone Duo and then disassembled the device to investigate. He found that the Duo’s hinge is more complex than a simple pivot, comprising a gear‑like central hinge and two different types of linking hinges.
summary: YouTuber CuriousHagi reproduced the cracked screen of the iPhone Duo during durability testing and dissected the device to investigate the issue. He found the Duo's hinge to be complex, consisting of a gear‑like central hinge and two different types of linking hinges, and believes the hinge is the cause of the cracks.
author: The Verge

title: More Palestinian families displaced in Hebron after shooting kills two Israeli soldiers
content: More Palestinian families have been displaced in the occupied West Bank as Israeli forces continue operations in Hebron, following a deadly shooting that killed two Israeli soldiers on Friday. With elections scheduled for Tuesday, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed a heavy response to the attack. Morgaene Ayre has the latest.
summary: More Palestinian families have been displaced in the occupied West Bank as Israeli forces continue operations in Hebron following a shooting that killed two Israeli soldiers on Friday. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed a heavy response ahead of elections scheduled for Tuesday, Morgaene Ayre reported.
author: France 24

title: Obama rallies Democratic candidates in Michigan and Ohio ahead of midterms
content:
Former President Barack Obama has begun a campaign‑trail push ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, visiting Michigan and Ohio to rally support for Democratic candidates. With less than two weeks remaining, he has called on voters to consider the rising cost of living, blaming the Trump administration and the White House for the economic pressures that concern many.

Democrats are hoping to regain control of Congress, and polls indicate several races are closely contested. Ophelie Jacobson has more.
summary: Former President Barack Obama has visited Michigan and Ohio to rally support for Democratic candidates ahead of the midterm elections. He criticized the Trump administration for rising living costs, a major concern for voters, as Democrats aim to regain control of Congress.
author: France 24

title: NFL holds first regular-season game in France at Paris' Stade de France
content: Paris’s Stade de France hosted its first NFL regular‑season game on Sunday, October 25, marking the sport’s debut in France. The matchup featured the New Orleans Saints against the Pittsburgh Steelers, drawing fans from New Orleans, Pittsburgh, France and other European nations, according to France 24’s Taise Parente and Stéphanie Trouillard.
summary: Paris's iconic Stade de France hosted the first NFL regular-season game in France on Sunday, October 25. The Saints and the Steelers attracted fans from New Orleans and Pittsburgh, as well as from France and other European countries.
author: France 24

title: Brazil run-off between President Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro remains too close
content: Brazil’s presidential run‑off pits the country’s left‑wing President Lula against right‑wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro. The contest is described as a “coin‑flip” with little separating the two candidates, and the final results are expected to be known within a few hours.
summary: The run-off election in Brazil is a coin-flip, with little separating left-wing President Lula and right-wing rival Flávio Bolsonaro. The final results are expected to be clear in a few hours.
author: France 24

title: Marine Le Pen speaks at Orléans Zénith amid 10,000 anti‑Le Pen protesters
content:
Marine Le Pen addressed a crowd at the Zénith Arena in Orléans just before 4:30 p.m., under the stadium’s strobe lights. The radical‑right leader, who analysts say is on the doorstep of the presidency, spoke to a base that remains deeply and increasingly popular, having topped French popularity polls for months.

The event followed a wave of protests across France. Over ten thousand anti‑Le Pen demonstrators gathered outside the venue the day before, underscoring the polarising nature of her leadership.
summary: Marine Le Pen took the stage just before half past four at the Zénith Arena in Orléans under stadium strobe lights. The rally followed nationwide protests that included over ten thousand anti‑Le Pen demonstrators outside the venue, and analysts say she is polarising yet increasingly popular and has topped French popularity polls for months.
author: France 24

title: Bulgaria's record low turnout triggers November 1 presidential run‑off
content: Record low voter turnout in Bulgaria has triggered a presidential run‑off scheduled for November 1. The election was marked by sharp divisions over Russia’s war in Ukraine and Sofia’s relations with the Kremlin.
summary: Record low voter turnout in Bulgaria has triggered a presidential run‑off scheduled for November 1. The election was marked by strong divisions over Russia’s war in Ukraine and Sofia’s relations with the Kremlin.

title: Prague exhibition honors over 1,400 Roma who fought Nazis in Czechoslovakia
content: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague now showcases the stories of these partisans and soldiers, whose fates had received little attention for decades.
summary: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of those partisans and soldiers, whose fates have received little attention for decades.
author: DW World

title: Four-year-old girl dies after falling from tower block in Barking, east London
content: A four-year‑old girl died after falling from a tower block on St Paul’s Road in Barking, east London. She was injured in the “falling from height” on Saturday and later died in hospital, according to the Metropolitan Police. Police said the incident is not believed to be suspicious.
summary: A four-year-old girl fell from a tower block on St Paul’s Road in Barking, east London. She was injured, later died in hospital, and police said the incident is not believed to be suspicious.
author: Guardian World

title: John Healey adopts defence‑style compartmentalisation to curb budget leaks
content:
The public has been informed that Chancellor John Healey has implemented defence-style “compartmentalisation” to prevent Treasury financial secrets from leaking, driven by concerns over market-sensitive disclosures. These military analogies emerged in mid-August, when the Telegraph reported that Healey was “on a war footing” to stop the drip of information that he believed had beleaguered his predecessor, Rachel Reeves.

However, significant policies have been heavily trailed in the media despite these secrecy measures. This contrast raises questions about whether Healey’s approach to budget secrecy has played out differently from past budgets, given the discrepancy between the reported strict controls and the extent of pre-budget media coverage.
summary: John Healey has introduced defence‑style “compartmentalisation” to protect Treasury budget details, saying he is on a war footing to stop leaks he says affected Rachel Reeves. Despite the secrecy, significant policies have been heavily reported in the media.
author: Guardian World

title: Cabinet split over Rosebank oilfield as Chancellor backs, energy secretary leans to reject
content: A cabinet split has emerged over the decision on drilling at the Rosebank oilfield. Chancellor John Healey has expressed support for the controversial North Sea project, while the ultimate decision rests with Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh. According to the Guardian, Fahnbulleh is leaning towards rejecting the Rosebank proposal after recently granting permission for the smaller Jackdaw gasfield. The differing positions highlight internal disagreement within the government over the future of the Rosebank development.
summary: A cabinet split has emerged over whether to approve drilling at the Rosebank oilfield, with Chancellor John Healey in favour of the project. Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh, who is ultimately in charge of the decision, is leaning towards rejecting it after granting permission for the smaller Jackdaw gasfield.
author: Guardian World

title: Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh enters UN secretary‑general race with Palestine endorsement
content:
Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh, who served as the United Arab Emirates’ ambassador to the United Nations and helped secure the delivery of humanitarian aid to Gaza, has entered the race to succeed António Guterres as UN secretary‑general. Nusseibeh, of Palestinian heritage, is widely noted for her advocacy of the Palestinian cause and a two‑state solution, and she has received the formal endorsement of the state of Palestine.

The candidacy has attracted criticism over the United Arab Emirates’ record on human‑rights issues and its involvement in Sudan, alongside the diplomatic support she enjoys from Palestine.
summary: Lana Nusseibeh, the United Arab Emirates’ former ambassador to the UN who helped secure humanitarian aid deliveries to Gaza, has entered the race to succeed António Guterres as UN secretary‑general. She has won the endorsement of the state of Palestine but faces criticism over the UAE’s human‑rights record and its involvement in Sudan.
author: Guardian World

title: Macron accused by unions of endangering French protest right with bill on vandal damage
content:
Trade unions have accused President Emmanuel Macron of endangering France’s constitutional right to protest by advancing a bill that would require demonstrators to pay for damage caused by vandalism, even when they are not personally responsible. Opponents argue that such liability could undermine the rule of law and benefit far‑right groups.

The legislation is being fast‑tracked as the government confronts a month‑long wave of protests, including high‑school students blockading schools to demand action on teacher absences, repairs to dilapidated facilities and reforms to the university admissions platform. Macron, who is set to leave office next spring, faces criticism over the proposed measures.
summary: Macron accused by unions of endangering French protest right with bill on vandal damage.
author: Guardian World

title: Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić concedes defeat in parliamentary election
content: Vučić’s 12-year reign looks to have been ended by record turnout of voters in election provoked by student-led protests Serbia’s veteran leader Aleksandar Vučić has conceded defeat to the student movement, ushering in a seismic political shift after two years of student-led protests gave rise to a fiercely contested parliamentary election. Speaking on Sunday, Vučić cited preliminary results that showed the student-backed protest movement surging ahead. “Based on a stratified sample, it is clear that we lost these elections,” Vučić told supporters at his party headquarters in Belgrade.
summary: Veteran Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić said on Sunday that, based on a stratified sample of preliminary results, his party had lost the fiercely contested parliamentary election. He attributed the outcome to a record voter turnout driven by a two‑year student‑led protest movement.
author: Guardian World

title: MPs to honor Helen Haines as parliament reconvenes; Hanson says One Nation cartoons remain
content: Follow live updates Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast Auditor-general examining if detention in Victorian police cells breaches human rights The Victorian auditor-general is investigating the detention of people in police cells, after Guardian Australia revealed the practice routinely led to the force breaching its own guidelines. Police cells are designed to hold people for short periods, such as after arrest and for bail hearings. However, in 2025 there were media reports of police holding prisoners in police cells beyond the recommended 14-day limit. When cells at one station are full, police may transport individuals to other stations. In some reported cases, police have transported individuals hundreds of kilometres away. It’s changed dramatically in my time. I’ve been here for almost 20 years and security has changed, and the federal police, in my experience, have been very, very responsive to our requests when there are threats or the possibility of me going to an event.
summary: MPs to honor Helen Haines as parliament reconvenes; Hanson says One Nation cartoons remain.
author: Guardian World

title: Brazil 2026 runoff: Lula da Silva faces Flávio Bolsonaro after first‑round upset
content: The incumbent president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, suffered a shock defeat in the first round and is now contesting a runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro, identified as the son of his convicted predecessor. Polls slated to close at 17:00 BRT (20:00 GMT) were extended by two hours, with some districts already having reported results.
summary: Brazil 2026 runoff: Lula da Silva faces Flávio Bolsonaro after first‑round upset.

title: Carrick's decision to drop Bruno Fernandes backfires at United
content:
Michael Carrick’s decision to omit captain Bruno Fernandes from Manchester United’s lineup against Bournemouth has proven to be a significant gamble. The article describes the move as a make-or-break moment for Carrick, whose position was already precarious, and notes that the strategy ultimately failed. While Carrick maintained that the exclusion was based on footballing reasons, the subsequent defeat to Como has intensified scrutiny on his leadership. The piece argues that Carrick should not bear sole responsibility for these institutional failures, suggesting that the club’s broader issues under its current leadership are the root cause of the team’s struggles.

The situation was further complicated by public disagreements between Carrick and his players. Carrick faced criticism for his handling of Fernandes, who had previously commented on the team’s lack of pressing in a Champions League match. In contrast, Lisandro Martínez retained his place in the team despite having recently described the director of football, Jason Wilcox, as a hindrance to the club. This disparity in squad management highlights the complex dynamics within the squad and the club’s hierarchy.
summary: Carrick dropped Bruno Fernandes in the match against Bournemouth, a move that did not succeed. Carrick criticized the manager after the defeat to Como and may face consequences for the decision.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Joe Marchant recalled to England training squad for Nations Championship
content:
Sale centre Joe Marchant has been recalled to England’s training squad for the upcoming Nations Championship, marking his first call-up since the 2023 World Cup. His selection comes as coach Steve Borthwick addresses injury concerns affecting the midfield. Marchant becomes available for selection following the conclusion of his two-year stint at Stade Français, which ended with his return to the Gallagher Premiership with Sale this season.

The 36-man squad also includes Gloucester’s Will Joseph, who is part of the group assembled for next month’s tournament.
summary: Joe Marchant has been recalled to Steve Borthwick’s 36‑man England training squad for next month’s Nations Championship as midfield options face injury disruption. The selection is his first England call‑up since the 2023 World Cup after returning to Sale from a two‑year spell at Stade Français.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Marcus Smith marks 200th Harlequins appearance as team beats Saracens 33-15
content: Harlequins 33-15 Saracens England fly-half marks 200th appearance in style Marcus Smith celebrated his 200th Harlequins match in magnificent style. Perhaps there is a danger, at times, of taking his immense talent for granted, but the 27-year-old was simply unstoppable here. A powerful visiting Saracens side barely got a look-in, with Smith giving a reminder of his prodigious ability on the day Steve Borthwick names his England squad for a packed November schedule. Smith’s sensational running, distribution and tactical kicking masterfully controlled Quins’ attack for a badly needed success. They were nought from three in the league, and this was a vital result for more important reasons than Smith’s personal prestige on a milestone occasion. Smith is marginally the youngest Harlequin to make it to 200 matches: a couple of months younger than Mike Brown.
summary: Marcus Smith celebrated his 200th match for Harlequins by leading his team to a 33-15 victory over Saracens. The 27-year-old England fly-half controlled the attack with powerful running and tactical kicking to secure a vital league win.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Liverpool ends Brighton's four-game winning streak with Isak goal
content:
Liverpool ended Brighton’s four-match Premier League winning streak at Anfield, securing a home victory for the first time this season. The hosts displayed urgency and appetite at both ends of the pitch, with the new signings of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak, and Bradley Barcola showing signs of adapting to manager Andoni Iraola’s methods. The match featured an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross, in which Wirtz was instrumental.

Alexander Isak provided the decisive finishing touch, scoring his sixth goal in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence. In the second half, Liverpool focused on defending their lead and box, with Barcola sprinting back to assist the defense and Ronald Araújo engaging in physical challenges. These defensive efforts satisfied Iraola as much as his team’s earlier incisiveness, establishing Liverpool as deserving winners on home soil.
summary: Liverpool defeated Brighton at Anfield, ending the visitors' four-game winning streak. Alexander Isak scored his sixth goal in six Premier League appearances and Florian Wirtz assisted the opening goal credited to Pascal Gross.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Shadab Khan's unbeaten 113 secures Pakistan's win over England
content:
England were stunned when Shadab Khan’s unbeaten 113 propelled Pakistan to a one‑wicket victory. The hosts had been 154 for nine, and with 88 runs still required Pakistan were on the brink of collapse. Shadab’s rapid boundary‑peppering turned the match into a thriller, and he and Haris Rauf secured the win.

Haris Rauf contributed seven runs from 19 balls, providing solid support for Shadab’s on‑rampage. A dramatic moment came when Shadab was initially given out lbw to a full toss on 97; he began to walk off, hands shaken with England, only for an inside edge to be discovered on review.

The result guarantees Pakistan a place in the tri‑series final, ending England’s chances of victory in the match.
summary: Shadab Khan scored an unbeaten 113 as Pakistan chased 154, winning by one wicket. Haris Rauf took seven wickets from 19 balls, and a review overturned an LBW dismissal.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Steelers beat Saints 16-10 in Paris
content: The Steelers defeated the Saints 16-10 in a game played in Paris. In another matchup, the Browns, currently 0-7, trailed the Titans late in the first quarter after a 36-yard rushing touchdown by T. Pollard. The Titans extended their lead with a seven-yard pass from M. Willis to C. Douglas and a 48-yard pass from T. Huntley to Z. Flowers.
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in a game played in Paris. The Steelers held off the Saints for the entire contest.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Michael Carrick on brink after Manchester United humiliated by Bournemouth
content: After Bruno Fernandes was dropped for “pure football” reasons – according to Michael Carrick – could ­Manchester United actually win a game of football? The answer, again, was a resounding, humiliating no, and if the manager’s job remains in real peril, you have to wonder, too, if this beleaguered team should steel itself for a relegation dogfight. They lack imagination, cohesion, fight, confidence and anything resembling joy, and so now hovering a point above the drop zone, survival cannot be taken for granted.
summary: Bruno Fernandes was dropped for “pure football” reasons, leaving Manchester United humiliated by Bournemouth. The club now sits just above the drop zone, with the manager's job in real peril and the team lacking imagination, cohesion, fight, confidence, and joy.
author: Guardian Sport

content: Melvine Malard scored twice and secured a penalty, helping Chelsea overturn a deficit to win 3‑1 over Crystal Palace in the Women’s Super League. The match, played away, saw Chelsea extend their unbeaten start to seven games this season.

title: Jarman wins historic second Worlds silver in vault final

summary: Jake Jarman becomes the first British male gymnast to win two individual medals at a World Gymnastics Championships, landing silver in a thrilling men's vault final in Rotterdam.

content: Alexander Isak scored his sixth Premier League goal of the season, a performance described as finally living up to his price tag. The result marked Liverpool's fourth victory in their last four matches under manager Andoni Iraola, rewarding the club's patience with the striker.

title: Axelrod Criticizes Trump’s “I Don’t Give a Damn” Comment on Gas Prices
content: Democratic strategist David Axelrod criticized President Trump’s Saturday evening rally remarks, where Trump stated he “did not give a damn” about high fuel prices because “we’re making a freaking fortune” on oil. Axelrod argued that this statement is not a winning message, noting that Trump is making unprecedented money while disregarding the impact of high prices on supporters.
summary: Democratic strategist David Axelrod criticized President Trump for saying he did not care about high fuel prices because he was making a fortune on oil. Axelrod said the remark was not a winning message.

title: Ted Brown denies taking votes from Paxton in Texas Senate race
content: Ted Brown, the Libertarian candidate in the Texas Senate race, rejected claims that his presence splits votes and could cost Republican Ken Paxton the election. Brown noted that both political sides are making similar accusations regarding his potential impact on the race.
summary: Ted Brown, the Libertarian candidate in the Texas Senate race, says he is not taking votes away from Attorney General Ken Paxton or Democrat Talarico. He dismisses claims that his candidacy could split the vote and cost Paxton the election.
